html:
The Ngaun, or Ngawun, were an Aboriginal Australian people of the inland plains of northwest Queensland, south of the Gulf of Carpentaria. The map shows them from 1600 to 1800.

Almost nothing is recorded of them beyond their name and the rough bounds of their land. Neighbours on the map include the Wunumara, the Mayi Thakurti and the Mayi Kulan. Cattle stations spread over these grasslands from the 1860s, and many small peoples of the region lost their land and much of their population within a generation. See Aboriginal Australian societies.
